title: Pantoprazole in patients at risk for gastrointestinal bleeding in the ICU
authors: Krag M, Marker S, Perner A, Wetterslev J, Wise MP, Schefold JC, et al.
followUp: 90 days; 1 year for mortality in the registry results
population: Adults with unplanned ICU admission at risk of gastrointestinal bleeding in six European countries; intravenous pantoprazole 40 mg daily or placebo during the ICU stay
funder: Abstract: 'Funded by Innovation Fund Denmark and others.' Registry NCT02467621: lead sponsor Dr. Morten Hylander Møller (sponsor-investigator, Scandinavian Critical Care Trials Group); collaborators Copenhagen University Hospital, Rigshospitalet, and the Copenhagen Trial Unit. The full funding statement was not read because the publisher page refused access.
result: Death by 90 days: 510 of 1642 (31.1%) with pantoprazole against 499 of 1640 (30.4%) with placebo (RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.91 to 1.13). Composite of clinically important bleeding, pneumonia, C. difficile infection or myocardial ischaemia: 21.9% against 22.6% (RR 0.96, 0.83 to 1.11). Clinically important gastrointestinal bleeding 41 of 1644 (2.5%) against 69 of 1647 (4.2%). Infectious adverse events 276 against 279; 1-year mortality 610 of 1635 against 601 of 1626 (registry results).
